newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields lower on May CPI figure.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields lower on May CPI figure.

text.p: Swedish bond yields were lower at midday on Thursday, supported by a lower than expected May consumer price index (CPI) figure.
Consumer prices were flat in May compared to April while market players had targeted a rise of 0.1 percent. Year-on-year, CPI rose 0.3 percent.
"Yields came down on a lower than expected CPI combined with yesterday's somewhat weaker than expected GDP figure," a trader said, adding that the figures had reduced inflation fears.
GDP fell 0.3 percent in the first quarter from the previous quarter but rose 1.6 percent from the first quarter last year.
The six-month T-bill slipped two basis points to 4.18 percent and the ten-year bond yield fell three to 6.90 percent.
The crown firmed to 4.5120 against the mark from 4.5260 late on Wednesday, supported by a stronger dollar and a generally softer mark.
"The mark has weakened against (currencies in) high-yielding countries," one dealer said.
News of investment company Incentive's sale of half its stake in ABB AB could boost the crown as there may be foreign buyers, one dealer said.
